title: Coordinate independence of polynomial parts
statement: Let $F$ be a real coefficient family on subsets of $[n]$, let $i\in[n]$, let $\Omega$ be a type, and let $X,Y:[n]\to(\Omega\to\mathbb R)$. Suppose $X_j=Y_j$ as functions on $\Omega$ for every $j\ne i$. Then, as functions on $\Omega$, the random-input evaluations of the coordinate-free part of $F$ agree for $X$ and $Y$, and the random-input evaluations of the coefficient family formed from the Fourier coefficients of the Boolean-cube derivative of $F$ also agree for $X$ and $Y$.
hypotheses_covered: $F$ is a real coefficient family on subsets of $[n]$
$X,Y$ are families of real-valued functions on $\Omega$
